findings.summary: Tripwire audit RED on the ACTIVATED leg: integrity-guards declared activation.default 'on' while five of its nine shipped hooks (exitcode, overmock, exhaustive, flaky, redlock) were OFF, so capability_registry.py doctor printed a dark inventory that could not name them. Dark-to-the-OPERATOR is the section 6a class the registry exists to make impossible, and the registry was the thing hiding it. The user-facing switch existed; the health surface never said five guards were inert.

H7 selection-pattern warning, RECORDED rather than argued down: all ten debts swept in Phase 3 were VERIFICATION debts (gate-surface calibration for v1.24/v1.25/v1.26, two corpus-approval queues, Codex verifier calibration, the R3 premise-plant probe) and NONE was paid — ten became two, six weeks later — in the same release that retired five guards on yield data. Each move is individually defensible and each still fails loudly, but the pattern is that this release's deferrals removed calibration scope exclusively. Disposition: accepted as a finding, not remediated — the work needs a live claude binary and budget no session can supply, which is why the blocker is named in every re-dated entry, and advisory-guards-optin's 2026-11-15 debt is the mechanical re-read.

The release commit went GREEN locally and RED in CI. Cause: the local gate ran against the WORKING TREE while review_ledger's coverage check evaluates the COMMITTED HEAD, whose tail was not metadata-only. Recorded because it is the first live demonstration of what the new independent runner buys — the property the CIVerd retirement was justified on ('verified rather than asserted') catching a real divergence on its second real use, on the release commit itself.
